summary_paragraph: A female patient with systemic lupus erythematosus, antiphospholipid syndrome, end-stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis, and a history of renal transplant failure was admitted with a supratherapeutic INR of 19.1 following an ankle fracture and episodes of hematemesis and epistaxis. She was treated with IV vitamin K, FFP, and pantoprazole, with successful reversal of anticoagulation. Her INR stabilized, and no active bleeding was observed. Hyperkalemia was managed with insulin and dextrose, and dialysis was adjusted. Confusion was attributed to uremia and metabolic imbalances. Chest pain was linked to peritoneal dialysis dwell volume. She was discharged home with a revised warfarin regimen, continued PPI therapy, and follow-up plans for INR monitoring and GI evaluation.
problems: Anticoagulants causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
